news.title: Fake Windows 11 24H2 Update Scam Steals Data — Patch Tuesday Tomorrow
news.excerpt: A convincing fake Windows 11 24H2 update page is circulating. It mimics a Microsoft support site, uses a believable cumulative-update name, and offers a blue download button for an 83 MB installer. The file is a malicious MSI built with legitimate tools that hides an infostealer

news.title: ClickFix fake browser updates are tricking people into running malware — close the tab
news.excerpt: That "Update Chrome" or "Update Firefox" page that pops up while you're browsing? It's a lie. ClickFix scams mimic real browser updates to get you to copy-paste a malicious command into your terminal. Real browsers update themselves automatically — they never ask you to run commands. Close the tab. If it won't close, hold your power button for 15 seconds until the screen goes black, then turn it back on.

news.title: Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell
news.excerpt:
Scammers Are Faking Official-Looking Notices — Here's the Tell.

You get an email or see a webpage that looks exactly like it's from
your bank, the IRS, or a government agency. The logo is perfect.
The formatting is perfect. It says "Immediate action required" and
threatens account closure, legal trouble, or lost benefits if you
don't respond today.

The giveaway: they ask for something no legitimate organization
would ever request by email. Your Social Security number. Your
bank login. A payment in gift cards or wire transfer. Remote access
to your computer.

Real banks and government agencies don't operate this way. They
already have your information. They don't threaten instant disaster.
They don't demand gift cards.

What to do: Don't click any links in the message. Don't call...

news.title: Password Manager Breach — mSecure Users Told to Change All Passwords
news.excerpt:
Password manager mSecure just told all users to change every password stored in their vault — but won't say what actually happened. On November 3, mSeven Software emailed customers about "suspicious activity" and said to immediately change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys. They didn't say when it happened, what was accessed, or if your data was stolen. Because the scope is unknown, assume the worst: change your most important passwords first (email, banking, work) through each service's official website. Use a different, strong password for each. Consider moving to a different password manager until mSecure explains what happened.

Source: Malwarebytes — November 4–6, 2026

news.title: That 'Gift Card Payment' Demand Is a Scam — Hang Up
news.excerpt:
The phone rings. The caller says you owe money — taxes, a utility bill, a court fine — and the only way to pay today is with gift cards. "Go to the store, buy Apple or Google Play cards, read me the numbers on the back."

No real government agency or legitimate company asks for gift cards. Ever. Gift cards are for gifts. Once you read the numbers, the money is gone and you can't get it back.

What to do: Hang up. If you're worried you owe something, look up the official number yourself and call. Never pay anyone with gift cards. Never read card numbers to anyone on the phone.

The rule: Gift cards are for presents. If someone demands them as payment, it's a scam. Every single time.

Source: FTC.gov — October 2026

posts.title: Fake Antivirus Renewal Emails Steal Your Credit Card — Check Subscription Status Directly in the App
posts.summary: If an email says your Norton or McAfee subscription renewed for $80–$100, don't click the link. Open the security app on your computer or go to norton.com / mcafee.com directly to check your real status.
posts.truth: This scam works because antivirus renewals are confusing — the product came with the PC, someone else manages it, or you forgot. The email exploits that uncertainty. Check subscription status directly in the app at norton.com or mcafee.com, never via an email link.
